candidate.blueprint_topic: Management of Care — quality measurement and performance improvement
candidate.educational_objective: Use quality dashboards to make selected performance measures, gaps, and trends against goals visible for monitoring and shared improvement work rather than treating the display itself as proof of causation or root-cause analysis.

options.A: It establishes the exact root cause of every adverse event without any additional event investigation.
options.B: It removes the need to select measures that are linked to the improvement goal and intervention.
options.C: It proves that any change in a metric was caused by the most recent intervention, regardless of other factors.
options.D: It summarizes important performance data so staff can identify gaps and trends against goals and share consistent information across organizational levels.

candidate.rationale: AHRQ states that dashboard reports present important data in summary form to make gaps in performance and trends against goals easier to identify and can share consistent information across multiple organizational levels. Therefore D is correct. A dashboard does not by itself establish root causes, so A is incorrect. B conflicts with AHRQ's requirement to choose measures linked to the improvement goal and intervention. C overstates what a dashboard can establish; AHRQ describes monitoring how interventions relate to changes, not proof that one intervention caused every observed change.
candidate.source_claim_supported: AHRQ recommends selecting measures tied to improvement goals and interventions, visualizing and monitoring performance, and using dashboard reports to summarize data, identify gaps and trends against goals, and share consistent information across organizational levels.
